note: The INI parser copies the attacker-controlled description line into the job option array.
fio duplicates the parsed options before substitution and parsing.
The copied description option is handed to keyword replacement.
The function finds the $ncpus keyword inside the option string.
A heap buffer is allocated for the rewritten string.
The source pointer is advanced past the keyword, so later tail copying uses a shifted pointer.
The original allocation is freed while the function still relies on the shifted opt pointer, which is the root cause of the heap-buffer-overflow described in the issue.
